transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-08
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Alex Romero (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (Redwood SE); Dana Lee, Raj Patel, Marta Alvarez, Tom Green (Marigold Health)

Summary:
Quick scoping for a security-focused POC/pilot to validate Redwood Dedicated + Private options. Discussed workload sizing, benchmarks, timelines, and specific security/compliance requirements (SOC 2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS). Agreed to exchange security pack, sample workload, and schedule bench week of 2027-12-20.

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm alex romero from redwood, i'm the AE on this - quick intros?
[00:10] Dana: dana lee, head of eng at marigold, thanks, excited to chat.
[00:15] Raj: raj, secops, i'll be driving the compliance checklist.
[00:20] Priya: priya nair, solutions eng - i'll handle the bench and SSO setup.
[00:25] Tom: tom green, cto, i'll be listening for timelines and risk.

[02:05] Alex: great, the goal today is to scope the pilot: what success looks like, what workloads you want us to run, security gates - SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO and RBAC needs, audit log granularity, and timeline to go from pilot to proof.

[03:00] Marta: high level, we want a secure hosted option but need to validate both the dedicated/reserved and private (vpc) nuancing. Primary use case is clinician-assist summarization and triage: bursts of requests from EHR integrations, qps about 20-40, 95th latency target under 600ms for short prompts but up to 2s for longer context. Cost sensitivity is there but security and auditability are blockers.

[04:12] Priya: ok can you give ballpark input sizes - average token lengths and typical concurrency?
[04:20] Marta: typical prompt 150-400 tokens, often with 2-3k context pulled in for patient history but we can test incremental KV caching. Concurrent sessions roughly 15-30 active, spikes to 80 during shift changes.

[06:30] Jordan: noted - for benchmarking we'll exercise average, heavy context (2-3k), and spike patterns. we'll produce a plan that mirrors your seq length distribution.

[07:15] Raj: on security, first, SOC 2 and ISO27001 - do you have certificates and can you share scoping and any exceptions? We need evidence for our audit.
[07:40] Alex: yes we are SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 certified; i'll send the certs and the security pack with the scope, control mappings, and SOC attestation redactions. link will be in the follow-up.

[08:05] Raj: good. next, SSO - we enforce SAML 2.0 with our IdP (Okta). We need test SAML metadata, ability to map groups to roles, and session expiry controls.
[08:25] Priya: we support SAML and OIDC; for the pilot we can set up a staging SAML connection. we also support group-to-role mapping in our console and can demonstrate RBAC controls. i'll share the metadata and a checklist of assertions we expect (nameid, groups, email).

[09:05] Raj: audit logs are critical - we need immutable logs for all API calls, who accessed what model/route, token-level cost attribution, and export capability to our SIEM (S3 or syslog). retention needs to be 1 year for pilot evidence, longer if we go to prod.
[09:30] Alex: our console has per-request audit logs, routing, and token usage traces; we can export logs to S3 and stream to your SIEM. retention and export policies are configurable on Private/Dedicated. we'll include an example log schema in the pack.

[11:00] Tom: what about encryption and KMS/HSM integration? we need CMEK and customer-managed keys for sensitive PII content.
[11:20] Priya: we support KMS integration for private deployments; for hosted we have envelope encryption and can integrate with customer KMS for certain plans. for Dedicated/Private we'll walk through HSM/KMS setup in the pilot.

[12:40] Marta: data residency - our patient data must remain in US regions. can you guarantee region pinning for dedicated nodes?
[12:55] Alex: yes, we support region pinning; for private deployment we can ensure all inference happens in your VPC in us-west-2, and control planes can be configured per agreement.

[14:10] Raj: any third-party subprocessors? we need a list for our DPA.
[14:20] Alex: we'll include subprocessors in the security packet; standard cloud infra vendors plus our compute partners.

[15:30] Priya: on the bench plan — we'll run three workloads: baseline (avg prompts), heavy context (2-3k tokens), and spike test (burst to 80 qps). we'll measure p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, cost per 1k tokens, and quality regression on your eval set.

[16:10] Marta: for quality, we'll run 200 representative prompts and expect less than 5% regression vs current baseline. we can share labeled examples.

[17:00] Jordan: can you share sample payloads and example tokens? we need them to shape batching and cache strategies.
[17:10] Marta: yes we'll anonymize and send by 12/15.

[18:20] Priya: timeline proposal: send security pack and bench plan by 12/10-12/14, Marigold provides samples and IdP staging by 12/15, we run bench week of 12/20, then review on 12/22 for go/no-go to expanded pilot in Jan. Thoughts?

[18:40] Tom: sounds reasonable, need to confirm internal budget but that's fine.

[20:00] Raj: RBAC detail - we need at least three roles: admin, auditor (read-only logs), and operator (deploy/rollout). audit role must not have access to secrets. also support SCIM for group sync eventually.

[20:30] Priya: we support admin/operator/auditor patterns and SCIM; for the pilot we'll do group-to-role mapping via SAML and can add SCIM later.

[22:05] Alex: on success criteria - Marta, can you outline thresholds?
[22:12] Marta: yes - latency: p95 under 1.5s for heavy context, p95 <600ms for short prompts; cost target: reduce cost per interaction vs our current hosted vendor by at least 20%; accuracy/regression: <5% drop; operational: SSO + audit export validated; security: SOC2 artifacts received and no blockers from secops.

[24:40] Jordan: for benchmarks we'll include identical request streams to ensure apples-to-apples; we can run your existing vendor in parallel if you can provide keys/consent.

[25:10] Raj: we may not share keys but can replay traces; also we'll need to ensure logs don't include PHI in transit; redact PII in logs or use tokenization.

[26:00] Priya: agreed — we can configure redaction/pseudonymization for logs and show that data at rest is encrypted.

[28:15] Alex: pricing/pilot scope - typically we run a 2-4 week pilot on Dedicated or Private with a modest commit for reserving capacity; we'll provide estimated cost after we see your traces.

[29:10] Tom: what's the minimum lead time to spin up dedicated nodes or private?
[29:25] Priya: dedicated pool usually 3-5 business days once capacity is confirmed; private (VPC) can be 2-3 weeks depending on networking and KMS/HSM setup. for pilot we can often do a hybrid — dedicated within our cloud region pinned to your org.

[31:05] Marta: who owns data retention and deletion flows? for example, logs vs payloads?
[31:20] Alex: we default to ephemeral inference cache unless you opt-in to retention; for pilot we'll set retention to 30 days for payloads and 1 year for audit logs as per your ask, and show the deletion flow.

[33:00] Raj: legal/DPAs - we'll need a DPA and BAA (HIPAA) addendum if there's PHI involved. is Redwood willing to sign?
[33:15] Alex: yes, we have a standard BAA template for healthcare customers; legal can start that in parallel once we have the SOW. i'll flag legal.

[35:40] Jordan: for telemetry we provide token-level cost breakdowns and per-route traces; that will help you attribute to departments and clinicians.

[36:10] Marta: operational runbook — can you provide escalation contacts and SLA expectations for pilot?
[36:25] Alex: yes, we'll share a pilot runbook with contacts, SLAs (uptime for dedicated pilot), and escalation matrix.

[38:50] Priya: technical deep-dive note: if we see heavy KV cache benefit we'll enable prefix caching which should reduce latency for multi-turn dialogs. we'll measure cold vs warm latencies in bench.

[40:00] Raj: any automated rollbacks for model regressions? we need safe fallback to a smaller model if latency spikes or quality drops.
[40:15] Jordan: yep, our routing policies allow canary rollouts, automatic fallback to a compatible model variant, and circuit-breaker behaviour. we'll demo this in the pilot.

[42:05] Alex: ok let's recap next steps and owners — i'll send SOC2/ISO pack and subprocessors list; priya will send bench plan and SAML metadata; marigold will provide sample payloads, IdP staging, and success criteria matrix. we schedule bench week of 12/20 and follow-up on 12/22.

[44:20] Marta: one more question - what metrics do you surface for data access? we want to see which engineer or service invoked which model and for which patient id (pseudonymized).
[44:35] Priya: logs will include request id, user/service principal (from SAML assertion), model/route, and token usage. we can pseudonymize patient ids and include a mapping table that you control.

[46:00] Raj: ensure audit logs are tamper-evident — do you support append-only storage or signed logs?
[46:10] Alex: we can sign logs and use object lock in S3 or write to an append-only syslog sink; we'll include options in the security pack.

[48:00] Tom: ok, assume we greenlight this internally. pricing and SOW to follow, but security gating is critical.

[49:20] Alex: understood. we'll prioritize the security artifacts.

[50:30] Jordan: quick note on performance - for 2-3k context, the choice of model and quantization will matter; we'll recommend model variants and quantization profile after we see samples.

[52:00] Marta: for the pilot's success criteria matrix, i'll include business impact lines — e.g., 20% faster triage time and reduced clinician keystrokes — but technical thresholds as we said.

[53:30] Raj: last ask: can you provide a timeline for when full audit docs and control evidence will be in place? we need it to present to our auditors.

[53:45] Alex: i'll target 12/10 for the initial pack (certs, control mappings, subprocessors, log schema) and can follow with deeper artifacts post-bench.

[55:10] Alex: any final questions?
[55:20] Tom: none from me; thanks.
[55:25] Marta: no, thanks.
[55:30] Raj: thanks.

[56:00] Alex: great — recap email with attachments coming from me tomorrow; action items as we discussed. thanks everyone.

Attachments / referenced artifacts:
- SOC2 Type II cert (to be shared)
- ISO27001 cert (to be shared)
- Security pack + subprocessors list (link to be provided)
- Benchmark plan (Priya)
- Sample payloads (Marigold)

End of transcript.
